# Licensing + product analytics (Workroom app, CLI, and codaset)

## Context

This started as "what are the options for analytics in the Mac app" and turned into a licensing
project during review. That is the correct outcome, not scope creep: analytics needs an identity to
be worth much, licensing needs one for real product reasons, and once licensing exists analytics
rides it almost for free. Building analytics identity first would have been building the wrong thing.

**Where it began.** The app has no product analytics. Sentry is linked and running
(`Core/SentryConfig.swift`, started at `WorkroomApp.swift:19`) with crash reporting, hang tracking,
tracing, profiling and metrics — but it answers "what broke", never "what gets used". Nothing tells
us whether jj or git dominates, whether the inspector's Files/PR panes earn their code, or whether
the `pre` channel has anyone on it.

**Where it landed.** Every install auto-registers a license key with codaset. The license enforces
usage limits. Behaviour events carry that key, so analytics is identified data, not anonymous.
The CLI enforces the same entitlement the app does.

### The decision trail (what this review changed)

| # | Decision | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| D3 | Snapshot only, no analytics install ID | superseded by licensing — a real identity now exists |
| D4 | Self-hosted, no third-party SDK | stands — codaset is the server |
| D5 | Emit at first successful `AppStore.load`, once-flag | stands for the snapshot |
| D6 | Hoist `BuildIdentity` out of `SentryConfig` | stands |
| D7 | One in-memory retry, then drop | stands, now paired with an idempotency key |
| D8 | `CountBucket` gains `.none` | **moved to licensing** — enforcement needs exact counts, not buckets |
| D9 | Emit only on a successful load | stands |
| D10 | Snapshot **and** coarse action events | stands |
| D11 | Design the endpoint now, in `../codaset` | stands |
| D13 | The CLI enforces the entitlement too | the CLI becomes licensed software |
| D14 | Behaviour events carry the license key | analytics is personal data, with everything that implies |
| D15 | ~7-day token TTL + **sticky** revocation | revocation bites on first contact, not at expiry |
| D16 | Over-limit is a **hard block** until under the limit | needs a deadlock-proof escape hatch |

## The blocker, stated plainly

**codaset is not deployed anywhere.** It has CI only — no Dockerfile, no Procfile, no Kamal or fly
config, and `config/environments/production.rb:60` still reads `host: 'example.com'`. Nothing in this
plan can ship until codaset is live. That is now the critical path, ahead of every client change.

## Architecture

```
  ┌─ Workroom.app (Swift) ──────────┐        ┌─ workroom CLI (Go) ───────────┐
  │  first launch → register        │        │  add-project → check          │
  │  behaviour events → POST        │        │  entitlement before creating  │
  └──────────────┬──────────────────┘        └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                 │                                           │
                 │   both read the SAME cached entitlement   │
                 │   (signed token on disk, offline grace)   │
                 └─────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                                   │ HTTPS, authenticated by license key
                                   ▼
              ┌─ codaset (Rails 8.1 / Postgres / Sidekiq) ─────────────┐
              │                                                        │
              │  licenses          identity, tier, limits, check-ins   │
              │    │                → install counts, retention,       │
              │    │                  version spread, project counts   │
              │    │                                                   │
              │    └──► analytics_events   license_id FK, event name,   │
              │                            typed properties, event_id   │
              │                              → behaviour, joinable      │
              └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Two tables, one identity, deliberately joined (D14). Licensing owns *who / how many / how long*;
analytics owns *what they did*. The join is what makes "which features do renewers use" answerable.

### What identified analytics costs, and must be paid

D14 traded anonymity for the renewal-correlation question. The bill:

- **The Settings toggle cannot say "anonymous."** Label it "Send usage data"; the caption must state
  plainly that it is linked to the license.
- **A privacy policy page is now required before ship**, not deferred. `website/` has none today.
- **Deletion path:** deleting or expiring a license must delete or de-identify its
  `analytics_events` rows. A foreign key with `on_delete: :cascade` is the floor.
- **Retention policy:** a fixed window with a recurring Sidekiq job that enforces it.
- **Lawful basis:** opt-out default-on for *identified* analytics is weaker than it was for
  anonymous. This is a live residual risk, flagged rather than re-litigated — it was decided
  up front and is the user's call.

## Phases

### Phase 0 — deploy codaset (blocking)

Pick a host, add deploy config, real `default_url_options`, a database, Redis for Sidekiq, and a
domain. Nothing else in this plan is reachable before this lands.

### Phase 1 — licensing server (codaset)

Rails 8.1 / Ruby 4.0.3 / Postgres, UUIDv7 PKs by default, Phlex views, minitest + `fixture_kit`.
**codaset is a JJ repo — use `jj`, not `git`.** Rubocop enforces `Style/DisableSyntax`: no `unless`,
no `and`/`or`/`not`, no numbered block params; endless methods and hash shorthand are the house style;
`# frozen_string_literal: true` is implicit and must NOT be added.

- `License` model — key, tier, **server-controlled limits**, `revoked_at`, `last_seen_at`,
  org/user association. Limits are server state, editable at any time; the client never decides them.
- `POST /api/licenses` — auto-register on first launch. Returns the key plus a **signed entitlement
  token** (tier + limits + expiry) the client caches.
- `POST /api/licenses/:key/check` — periodic re-validation, refreshes the token, updates
  `last_seen_at`, records version and project/workroom counts. This is where retention, install
  counts and version spread come from. It is also the channel that pushes **limit changes** and
  **revocation**: a revoked license returns an explicit revoked response, never merely a refusal to
  reissue.
- **Raising a limit** takes effect on the next check-in with no client change. **Lowering** one below
  current usage puts the client in the over-limit state (D16) — see Phase 3.
- Rate limiting: Rails 8's built-in `rate_limit to:, within:`, keyed by license key. Note it uses
  `Rails.cache`, and codaset sets no `cache_store` in `production.rb` — point it at the Redis already
  present for Sidekiq rather than the default file store.

### Phase 2 — shared entitlement reader (Go)

One package in the `workroom` repo, consumed by **both** the CLI and (via the CLI's `--json` API) the
app. This is the D13 decision: the engine that creates projects is the engine that checks the limit.

- Verifies the signed token offline (public key baked into the binary — a *verification* key, safe to
  ship, unlike a shared secret).
- Cached token on disk with a **~7-day TTL** (D15), because a dev tool must work on a plane. That
  number is the revocation-latency dial and the offline-tolerance dial at once; a week covers flights,
  conferences and a bad wifi stretch without leaving a month-long revocation hole.
- **Sticky revocation.** The first time the server reports revoked, that is written to disk
  permanently and never un-observed by a later offline period. Without this, revocation is opt-in by
  the person being revoked — they simply unplug and ride out the grace window. This is a security
  property, not a UX one: test that a revoked-then-offline client stays revoked across relaunch.
- Clock-skew tolerance; a clear "grace expired, reconnect to continue" state.

States the reader exposes, consumed identically by both products:
`unlicensed` · `active` · `over_limit` · `grace` · `expired` · `revoked`.

### Phase 3 — enforcement UX (app + CLI)

- `add-project` (and whichever action the tier limits) fails with a clear, actionable message naming
  the limit and how to lift it.
- **Over-limit is a hard block** (D16): the tool refuses the limited operations until the user is back
  under the limit. The copy must say what removal actually means — `delete-project` is **config-only**
  by default (`--from-disk` is opt-in), so unregistering a project leaves every file untouched on
  disk. "Remove a project from Workroom to continue. Your files stay where they are."
- **Deadlock escape hatch, load-bearing.** While blocked, `delete-project`, `list` and
  `delete-project --from-disk` must all keep working, and the app must still launch and render the
  sidebar. Otherwise the only way out of the block sits behind the block. Pin this with tests on both
  products — it is the single most likely way a hard block ships broken.
- The app surfaces the same state as UI, not a raw CLI error string.
- Both read one entitlement reader, so they cannot disagree about what is allowed.

### Phase 4 — analytics

**Snapshot** (D10), emitted at the end of the first *successful* `AppStore.load`
(`Core/AppStore.swift:2344`), guarded by a static once-flag. The flag is load-bearing:
`WorkroomApp.swift:54-59` documents that SwiftUI "mints one window — and one fresh `AppStore` — per
`WindowSeed`", and ⌘N opens a new seed. A failed load emits nothing and leaves the flag unset, so a
later successful reload can still emit (D9) — otherwise a broken CLI read would be recorded as a user
with no projects.

Set the flag **after** the consent check, not before, so enabling analytics later in the same process
is not permanently suppressed.

**Coarse action events** (D10) at real interaction points: inspector section opened, diff mode
switched, workroom created, VCS action run, pane split. Behaviour, not settings — the snapshot alone
measures configuration, which was Codex's sharpest hit.

**Typed payloads, no generic value container.** Codex is right that `AnalyticsValue.string(String)`
accepts any string, so a `[String: AnalyticsValue]` bag is not the compile-time guarantee the earlier
draft claimed. Each event case carries its own typed associated values — enums and integers only, no
free `String` — with an explicit wire encoder. That is what actually makes it impossible to attach a
repo path, branch, bookmark, workroom label, commit message, file name or terminal line.

**Sink.** `URLSession` POST to codaset, authenticated by the license key. Constraints:

- **`URLSessionConfiguration.ephemeral`, caching disabled.** A default session uses the shared URL
  cache, cookie storage and credential storage — a real defect Codex caught in the earlier draft.
- One in-memory retry after a short delay, then silent drop (D7). Launch is exactly when the network
  is least likely to be up (cold wake, wifi reconnecting), so a single attempt would systematically
  lose that whole category rather than a random sample.
- **A per-emit random `event_id`** (generated in memory, never persisted) sent as an idempotency key,
  with a unique index server-side. Without it the retry double-counts whenever the server accepted the
  first POST but the response was lost.
- Off the main thread. Never surfaces an error to the user.

**Counts are licensing's job now.** Enforcement cannot cap what it does not count, so project and
workroom counts arrive with the license check-in as exact numbers. Analytics does not carry them, and
`CountBucket` is not needed (D8 superseded).

### Testability — inject the seams

Codex is right that compile-time build flavour, `XCTest` env detection and global statics make
"every branch" untestable as drafted. `Analytics` takes injected **build identity**, **consent
provider**, **sink factory** and **launch-session state**, defaulting to the real ones. Same seam
`SentryConfig.defaultEnvironment(nightly:debug:)` already uses (`SentryConfig.swift:67`), and the same
reason `UITestFixture` exists.

## Failure modes

| Path | Failure | Test | Handled | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Registration | Offline on first launch | yes | grace/unregistered state | clear state, app still works |
| Entitlement | Token expired, still offline | yes | grace window, then block | "reconnect to continue" |
| Entitlement | Tampered token | yes | signature verify fails | treated as unlicensed |
| Entitlement | Revoked, then goes offline | yes | sticky revocation flag | stays revoked |
| Entitlement | Limit lowered below usage | yes | `over_limit` hard block | "remove a project to continue" |
| Enforcement | Blocked with no way out | yes | delete/list stay allowed | escape hatch works |
| Enforcement | CLI and app disagree | yes | one shared reader | n/a by construction |
| Analytics emit | Fires twice via ⌘N | yes | once-flag | nothing (correct) |
| Analytics emit | Load failed ⇒ zero counts | yes | no emit, flag unset | nothing (correct) |
| Sink | Cold wake, no wifi | yes | 1 retry, drop | nothing — silent by design |
| Sink | Response lost after accept | yes | `event_id` idempotency | nothing |
| Ingest | Flooded by a script | yes | per-key rate limit | nothing |

**Critical gap:** the grace-window design is not yet specified in enough detail to test — how long,
what happens at expiry, whether existing workrooms stay usable. That is a licensing design question,
not an analytics one, and it must be answered before Phase 2 is buildable.

107	  **revocation**: a revoked license returns an explicit revoked response, never merely a refusal to
108	  reissue.
109	- **Raising a limit** takes effect on the next check-in with no client change. **Lowering** one below
110	  current usage puts the client in the over-limit state (D16) — see Phase 3.
111	- Rate limiting: Rails 8's built-in `rate_limit to:, within:`, keyed by license key. Note it uses
112	  `Rails.cache`, and codaset sets no `cache_store` in `production.rb` — point it at the Redis already
113	  present for Sidekiq rather than the default file store.
114	
115	### Phase 2 — shared entitlement reader (Go)
116	
117	One package in the `workroom` repo, consumed by **both** the CLI and (via the CLI's `--json` API) the
118	app. This is the D13 decision: the engine that creates projects is the engine that checks the limit.
119	
120	- Verifies the signed token offline (public key baked into the binary — a *verification* key, safe to
121	  ship, unlike a shared secret).
122	- Cached token on disk with a **~7-day TTL** (D15), because a dev tool must work on a plane. That
123	  number is the revocation-latency dial and the offline-tolerance dial at once; a week covers flights,
124	  conferences and a bad wifi stretch without leaving a month-long revocation hole.
125	- **Sticky revocation.** The first time the server reports revoked, that is written to disk
126	  permanently and never un-observed by a later offline period. Without this, revocation is opt-in by
127	  the person being revoked — they simply unplug and ride out the grace window. This is a security
128	  property, not a UX one: test that a revoked-then-offline client stays revoked across relaunch.
129	- Clock-skew tolerance; a clear "grace expired, reconnect to continue" state.
130	
131	States the reader exposes, consumed identically by both products:
132	`unlicensed` · `active` · `over_limit` · `grace` · `expired` · `revoked`.
133	
134	### Phase 3 — enforcement UX (app + CLI)
135	
136	- `add-project` (and whichever action the tier limits) fails with a clear, actionable message naming
137	  the limit and how to lift it.
138	- **Over-limit is a hard block** (D16): the tool refuses the limited operations until the user is back
139	  under the limit. The copy must say what removal actually means — `delete-project` is **config-only**
140	  by default (`--from-disk` is opt-in), so unregistering a project leaves every file untouched on
141	  disk. "Remove a project from Workroom to continue. Your files stay where they are."
142	- **Deadlock escape hatch, load-bearing.** While blocked, `delete-project`, `list` and
143	  `delete-project --from-disk` must all keep working, and the app must still launch and render the
144	  sidebar. Otherwise the only way out of the block sits behind the block. Pin this with tests on both
145	  products — it is the single most likely way a hard block ships broken.
146	- The app surfaces the same state as UI, not a raw CLI error string.
147	- Both read one entitlement reader, so they cannot disagree about what is allowed.
148	
149	### Phase 4 — analytics
150	
151	**Snapshot** (D10), emitted at the end of the first *successful* `AppStore.load`
152	(`Core/AppStore.swift:2344`), guarded by a static once-flag. The flag is load-bearing:
153	`WorkroomApp.swift:54-59` documents that SwiftUI "mints one window — and one fresh `AppStore` — per
154	`WindowSeed`", and ⌘N opens a new seed. A failed load emits nothing and leaves the flag unset, so a
155	later successful reload can still emit (D9) — otherwise a broken CLI read would be recorded as a user
156	with no projects.
157	
158	Set the flag **after** the consent check, not before, so enabling analytics later in the same process
159	is not permanently suppressed.
160	
161	**Coarse action events** (D10) at real interaction points: inspector section opened, diff mode
162	switched, workroom created, VCS action run, pane split. Behaviour, not settings — the snapshot alone
163	measures configuration, which was Codex's sharpest hit.
164	
165	**Typed payloads, no generic value container.** Codex is right that `AnalyticsValue.string(String)`
166	accepts any string, so a `[String: AnalyticsValue]` bag is not the compile-time guarantee the earlier
167	draft claimed. Each event case carries its own typed associated values — enums and integers only, no
168	free `String` — with an explicit wire encoder. That is what actually makes it impossible to attach a
169	repo path, branch, bookmark, workroom label, commit message, file name or terminal line.
170	
171	**Sink.** `URLSession` POST to codaset, authenticated by the license key. Constraints:
172	
173	- **`URLSessionConfiguration.ephemeral`, caching disabled.** A default session uses the shared URL
174	  cache, cookie storage and credential storage — a real defect Codex caught in the earlier draft.
175	- One in-memory retry after a short delay, then silent drop (D7). Launch is exactly when the network
176	  is least likely to be up (cold wake, wifi reconnecting), so a single attempt would systematically
177	  lose that whole category rather than a random sample.
178	- **A per-emit random `event_id`** (generated in memory, never persisted) sent as an idempotency key,
179	  with a unique index server-side. Without it the retry double-counts whenever the server accepted the
180	  first POST but the response was lost.
181	- Off the main thread. Never surfaces an error to the user.
182	
183	**Counts are licensing's job now.** Enforcement cannot cap what it does not count, so project and
184	workroom counts arrive with the license check-in as exact numbers. Analytics does not carry them, and
185	`CountBucket` is not needed (D8 superseded).
186	
187	### Testability — inject the seams
188	
189	Codex is right that compile-time build flavour, `XCTest` env detection and global statics make
190	"every branch" untestable as drafted. `Analytics` takes injected **build identity**, **consent
191	provider**, **sink factory** and **launch-session state**, defaulting to the real ones. Same seam
192	`SentryConfig.defaultEnvironment(nightly:debug:)` already uses (`SentryConfig.swift:67`), and the same
193	reason `UITestFixture` exists.
194	
195	## Files
196	
197	**codaset** (JJ repo) — `app/models/license.rb`, `app/models/analytics_event.rb`,
198	`app/controllers/api/licenses_controller.rb`, `app/controllers/api/analytics_controller.rb`,
199	migrations, a retention job, deploy config, `config/routes.rb`.
200	
201	**workroom CLI (Go)** — new `internal/license/` (token verify, cache, grace), enforcement in
202	`internal/workroom/` create paths and `cmd/add-project`.
203	
204	**macapp** — `Core/BuildIdentity.swift` (hoisted from `SentryConfig`), `Core/AnalyticsEvent.swift`,
205	`Core/Analytics.swift`, `Core/AnalyticsHTTPSink.swift`, `Core/LicenseState.swift`; edits to
206	`Core/DefaultsKeys.swift`, `Core/SentryConfig.swift`, `Core/AppStore.swift:2344`,
207	`Views/SettingsView.swift:178`. New Swift files need `make app-generate`.
208	
209	**website** — a privacy policy page, linked from the app.
210	
211	## Tests
212	
213	- **REGRESSION (mandatory):** hoisting `defaultEnvironment` out of `SentryConfig` modifies working
214	  behaviour. Moved tests keep asserting all three outputs, plus one pinning that nightly still tags
215	  `nightly` — that mislabelling is the documented WORKROOM-2B confusion (`SentryConfig.swift:57-63`).
216	- **Go:** entitlement token verify (valid / tampered / expired / clock-skewed), TTL expiry, enforcement
217	  at the limit boundary (n-1, n, n+1), offline behaviour, **sticky revocation survives relaunch while
218	  offline**, **limit lowered below usage enters `over_limit`**, and — critically —
219	  **`delete-project` and `list` still work while blocked** (the deadlock escape hatch).
220	- **Rails (minitest + `fixture_kit`):** register, re-register idempotency, check-in updates
221	  `last_seen_at`, a limit edit reaches the next token, a revoked license returns an explicit revoked
222	  response, rate limit trips, unknown event name rejected, unknown property key rejected, duplicate
223	  `event_id` rejected, cascade delete removes a license's events, retention job deletes past the
224	  window.
225	- **Swift:** consent off ⇒ spy sink never called and no session constructed; debug and XCTest ⇒ noop;
226	  once-flag set after the consent check, not before; failed load ⇒ no emit and flag unset; every event
227	  case encodes to a stable name; `URLProtocol`-stubbed sink for 200 / non-2xx / transport error /
228	  retry-succeeds / teardown-before-retry.
229	- **XCUITest**, scoped to the new class only (never the full suite; `make app-uitest` ignores
230	  `APP_TEST_FLAGS`, so call `xcodebuild -only-testing:<Class>/<method>`): the Settings toggle flips
231	  and persists, matched by `accessibilityIdentifier` — XCUITest cannot match a `Form` `Toggle` by
232	  label.
233	
234	## Failure modes
235	
236	| Path | Failure | Test | Handled | User sees |
237	|---|---|---|---|---|
238	| Registration | Offline on first launch | yes | grace/unregistered state | clear state, app still works |
239	| Entitlement | Token expired, still offline | yes | grace window, then block | "reconnect to continue" |
240	| Entitlement | Tampered token | yes | signature verify fails | treated as unlicensed |
241	| Entitlement | Revoked, then goes offline | yes | sticky revocation flag | stays revoked |
242	| Entitlement | Limit lowered below usage | yes | `over_limit` hard block | "remove a project to continue" |
243	| Enforcement | Blocked with no way out | yes | delete/list stay allowed | escape hatch works |
244	| Enforcement | CLI and app disagree | yes | one shared reader | n/a by construction |
245	| Analytics emit | Fires twice via ⌘N | yes | once-flag | nothing (correct) |
246	| Analytics emit | Load failed ⇒ zero counts | yes | no emit, flag unset | nothing (correct) |
247	| Sink | Cold wake, no wifi | yes | 1 retry, drop | nothing — silent by design |
248	| Sink | Response lost after accept | yes | `event_id` idempotency | nothing |
249	| Ingest | Flooded by a script | yes | per-key rate limit | nothing |
250	
251	**Critical gap:** the grace-window design is not yet specified in enough detail to test — how long,
252	what happens at expiry, whether existing workrooms stay usable. That is a licensing design question,
253	not an analytics one, and it must be answered before Phase 2 is buildable.
254	
255	## NOT in scope
256	
257	- **CLI analytics** — the CLI enforces licensing but emits no behaviour events. Explicit non-goal.
258	- **Anonymous analytics** — D14 chose identified. The anonymity posture from D3/D4 is superseded.
259	- **Gating `SentryConfig.start()` behind a user toggle** — crash reporting stays unconditional with no
260	  user control. Raised in review and **explicitly declined** (D17), not deferred. Do not re-raise.
261	  If it is ever revisited: the gate must wrap the `start()` call itself, never filter events, because
262	  the crash handler installs before anything can crash (`SentryConfig.swift:16-20`).
263	- **Pricing and tier design** — this plan assumes limits exist; it does not choose them.
264	- **A licensing design review** — this was an analytics review that discovered licensing. Phases 0-3
265	  deserve their own `/plan-eng-review` before implementation.
266	
267	## What already exists (reused, not rebuilt)
268	
269	| Need | Existing code | Reused? |
270	|---|---|---|
271	| Build identity | `SentryConfig.swift:67`, `:76` | Yes — hoisted to `BuildIdentity` |
272	| Privacy-gate pattern (off ⇒ no request) | `loadRemoteAvatars`, `DefaultsKeys.swift:101` | Yes |
273	| Nightly identity | `ReleaseChannel.isNightlyBuild`, `ReleaseChannel.swift:67` | Yes |
274	| VCS kind per project | `Project.vcs`, `Models.swift:53` | Yes |
275	| Test-only seam | `XCTestConfigurationFilePath`, `WorkroomApp.swift:42` | Yes |
276	| Settings `Form` pane | `GeneralSettingsPane`, `SettingsView.swift:178` | Yes — no new pane |
277	| Log subsystem | `"com.developwithstyle.workroom"` (literal, `LibGit2.swift:28`) | Yes |
278	| App↔CLI transport | the `--json` envelope (`cmd/json.go`) | Yes — entitlement rides it |
279	| Rate limiting | Rails 8 built-in `rate_limit` | Yes — no gem |
280	| Generic CRUD | `ControllerConcerns::Crud` (codaset) | No — API ingest is not CRUD |
281	
282	## Parallelization
283	
284	| Lane | Steps | Modules | Depends on |
285	|---|---|---|---|
286	| — | Phase 0 deploy codaset | codaset deploy config | — |
287	| A | Phase 1 licensing server | codaset `app/`, `config/` | Phase 0 |
288	| B | `BuildIdentity` hoist + analytics schema | `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/` | — |
289	| C | Phase 2 entitlement reader | `internal/license/` (Go) | Phase 1 (token format) |
290	| D | Phase 3 enforcement + Phase 4 sink | `cmd/`, `internal/workroom/`, `macapp/` | B, C |
291	
292	**Launch B in parallel with Phase 0 + A** — it touches only `macapp/Core/` and needs no server. C
293	waits on A for the token format. D waits on both. Lanes B and D both touch `macapp/` — sequential
294	within that directory, so do not run them concurrently in separate worktrees.
295

304	5. End to end against a staging codaset: fresh install registers, entitlement caches, `add-project`

308	   (a hardcoded literal, NOT the bundle id — Debug and Release share it). Every property must be an

311	
312	Note the old `nettop shows zero connections` acceptance test is **void** — Sentry and the licensing
313	check-in both make network calls, so absence cannot be attributed to analytics. Verify at the

input.new_string:
### The second restriction dimension: release channels (issue #92)

Issue #92 names two restrictions, not one: **max projects** *and* **available release channels**.
The second has a different enforcement shape and was not covered above.

- The entitlement token must carry **allowed channels**, and `Updater.allowedChannels(for:)` must
  intersect its result with them rather than trusting `Defaults[.releaseChannel]` alone.
  `ReleaseChannel.pickerCases` (`ReleaseChannel.swift:52`) filters what the Settings picker offers.
- **Nightly is not a picker option — it is a separate product.** The `Nightly` build config has its
  own bundle id (`…workroom.nightly`), its own icon, its own DMG, and a `WorkroomReleaseChannel`
  Info.plist marker. Nobody reaches it through the picker; they download a different app. So gating
  nightly cannot happen in the picker at all.
- **GitHub Releases are public, so the download cannot be gated.** Anyone can fetch any DMG directly,
  Sparkle uninvolved. A channel restriction is therefore only enforceable **at run time**, by the
  entitlement check inside the running build — exactly the same conclusion as the CLI bypass (D13):
  *enforce where the software runs, not where it is fetched.* A nightly build whose license does not
  permit nightly must refuse to run (or degrade), because nothing stopped it being installed.
- The CLI has its own channel identity too — `main.channel` is baked at build time and
  `workroom update --channel` is user-facing — so the same gate applies there, per D13.

### Phase 3 — enforcement UX (app + CLI)

A cap enforced only in the GUI is defeated by one terminal command using the tool we ship alongside it. The entitlement reader has to be a shared Go package consumed by both products. 2. **codaset is not deployed** — CI only, no Dockerfile/Procfile/Kamal/fly config, and `config/environments/production.rb:60` still reads `host: 'example.com'`. That is the critical path, ahead of every client change. 3. **Channel restrictions can only be enforced at run time.** GitHub Releases are public, so any DMG can be fetched directly with Sparkle uninvolved, and Nightly is a separate product with its own bundle id rather than a picker option. Same conclusion as (1): enforce where the software runs, not where it is fetched. One decision left open: what "grace" means once the token TTL is 7 days. Phase 2 is not buildable until that is specified. ---
Full plan (click to expand) # Licensing + product analytics (Workroom app, CLI, and codaset) ## Context This started as "what are the options for analytics in the Mac app" and turned into a licensing project during review. That is the correct outcome, not scope creep: analytics needs an identity to be worth much, licensing needs one for real product reasons, and once licensing exists analytics rides it almost for free. Building analytics identity first would have been building the wrong thing. **Where it began.** The app has no product analytics. Sentry is linked and running (`Core/SentryConfig.swift`, started at `WorkroomApp.swift:19`) with crash reporting, hang tracking, tracing, profiling and metrics — but it answers "what broke", never "what gets used". Nothing tells us whether jj or git dominates, whether the inspector's Files/PR panes earn their code, or whether the `pre` channel has anyone on it. **Where it landed.** Every install auto-registers a license key with codaset. The license enforces usage limits. Behaviour events carry that key, so analytics is identified data, not anonymous. The CLI enforces the same entitlement the app does. ### The decision trail (what this review changed) | # | Decision | Consequence | |---|---|---| | D3 | Snapshot only, no analytics install ID | superseded by licensing — a real identity now exists | | D4 | Self-hosted, no third-party SDK | stands — codaset is the server | | D5 | Emit at first successful `AppStore.load`, once-flag | stands for the snapshot | | D6 | Hoist `BuildIdentity` out of `SentryConfig` | stands | | D7 | One in-memory retry, then drop | stands, now paired with an idempotency key | | D8 | `CountBucket` gains `.none` | **moved to licensing** — enforcement needs exact counts, not buckets | | D9 | Emit only on a successful load | stands | | D10 | Snapshot **and** coarse action events | stands | | D11 | Design the endpoint now, in codaset | stands | | D13 | The CLI enforces the entitlement too | the CLI becomes licensed software | | D14 | Behaviour events carry the license key | analytics is personal data, with everything that implies | | D15 | ~7-day token TTL + **sticky** revocation | revocation bites on first contact, not at expiry | | D16 | Over-limit is a **hard block** until under the limit | needs a deadlock-proof escape hatch | ## The blocker, stated plainly **codaset is not deployed anywhere.** It has CI only — no Dockerfile, no Procfile, no Kamal or fly config, and `config/environments/production.rb:60` still reads `host: 'example.com'`. Nothing in this plan can ship until codaset is live. That is now the critical path, ahead of every client change. ## Architecture ``` ┌─ Workroom.app (Swift) ──────────┐ ┌─ workroom CLI (Go) ───────────┐ │ first launch → register │ │ add-project → check │ │ behaviour events → POST │ │ entitlement before creating │ └──────────────┬──────────────────┘ └───────────────┬───────────────┘ │ │ │ both read the SAME cached entitlement │ │ (signed token on disk, offline grace) │ └─────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘ │ HTTPS, authenticated by license key ▼ ┌─ codaset (Rails 8.1 / Postgres / Sidekiq) ─────────────┐ │ │ │ licenses identity, tier, limits, check-ins │ │ │ → install counts, retention, │ │ │ version spread, project counts │ │ │ │ │ └──► analytics_events license_id FK, event name, │ │ typed properties, event_id │ │ → behaviour, joinable │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` Two tables, one identity, deliberately joined (D14). Licensing owns *who / how many / how long*; analytics owns *what they did*. The join is what makes "which features do renewers use" answerable. ### What identified analytics costs, and must be paid D14 traded anonymity for the renewal-correlation question. The bill: - **The Settings toggle cannot say "anonymous."** Label it "Send usage data"; the caption must state plainly that it is linked to the license. - **A privacy policy page is now required before ship**, not deferred. `website/` has none today. - **Deletion path:** deleting or expiring a license must delete or de-identify its `analytics_events` rows. A foreign key with `on_delete: :cascade` is the floor. - **Retention policy:** a fixed window with a recurring Sidekiq job that enforces it. - **Lawful basis:** opt-out default-on for *identified* analytics is weaker than it was for anonymous. Live residual risk, flagged rather than re-litigated. ## Phases ### Phase 0 — deploy codaset (blocking) Pick a host, add deploy config, real `default_url_options`, a database, Redis for Sidekiq, and a domain. Nothing else in this plan is reachable before this lands. ### Phase 1 — licensing server (codaset) Rails 8.1 / Ruby 4.0.3 / Postgres, UUIDv7 PKs by default, Phlex views, minitest + `fixture_kit`. **codaset is a JJ repo — use `jj`, not `git`.** Rubocop enforces `Style/DisableSyntax`: no `unless`, no `and`/`or`/`not`, no numbered block params; endless methods and hash shorthand are the house style; `# frozen_string_literal: true` is implicit and must NOT be added. - `License` model — key, tier, **server-controlled limits**, `revoked_at`, `last_seen_at`, org/user association. Limits are server state, editable at any time; the client never decides them. - `POST /api/licenses` — auto-register on first launch. Returns the key plus a **signed entitlement token** (tier + limits + expiry) the client caches. - `POST /api/licenses/:key/check` — periodic re-validation, refreshes the token, updates `last_seen_at`, records version and project/workroom counts. This is where retention, install counts and version spread come from. It is also the channel that pushes **limit changes** and **revocation**: a revoked license returns an explicit revoked response, never merely a refusal to reissue. - **Raising a limit** takes effect on the next check-in with no client change. **Lowering** one below current usage puts the client in the over-limit state (D16) — see Phase 3. - Rate limiting: Rails 8's built-in `rate_limit to:, within:`, keyed by license key. Note it uses `Rails.cache`, and codaset sets no `cache_store` in `production.rb` — point it at the Redis already present for Sidekiq rather than the default file store. ### Phase 2 — shared entitlement reader (Go) One package in the `workroom` repo, consumed by **both** the CLI and (via the CLI's `--json` API) the app. This is the D13 decision: the engine that creates projects is the engine that checks the limit. - Verifies the signed token offline (public key baked into the binary — a *verification* key, safe to ship, unlike a shared secret). - Cached token on disk with a **~7-day TTL** (D15), because a dev tool must work on a plane. That number is the revocation-latency dial and the offline-tolerance dial at once; a week covers flights, conferences and a bad wifi stretch without leaving a month-long revocation hole. - **Sticky revocation.** The first time the server reports revoked, that is written to disk permanently and never un-observed by a later offline period. Without this, revocation is opt-in by the person being revoked — they simply unplug and ride out the grace window. This is a security property, not a UX one: test that a revoked-then-offline client stays revoked across relaunch. - Clock-skew tolerance; a clear "grace expired, reconnect to continue" state. States the reader exposes, consumed identically by both products: `unlicensed` · `active` · `over_limit` · `grace` · `expired` · `revoked`. ### The second restriction dimension: release channels This issue names two restrictions, not one: **max projects** *and* **available release channels**. The second has a different enforcement shape. - The entitlement token must carry **allowed channels**, and `Updater.allowedChannels(for:)` must intersect its result with them rather than trusting `Defaults[.releaseChannel]` alone. `ReleaseChannel.pickerCases` (`ReleaseChannel.swift:52`) filters what the Settings picker offers. - **Nightly is not a picker option — it is a separate product.** The `Nightly` build config has its own bundle id (`…workroom.nightly`), its own icon, its own DMG, and a `WorkroomReleaseChannel` Info.plist marker. Nobody reaches it through the picker; they download a different app. So gating nightly cannot happen in the picker at all. - **GitHub Releases are public, so the download cannot be gated.** Anyone can fetch any DMG directly, Sparkle uninvolved. A channel restriction is therefore only enforceable **at run time**, by the entitlement check inside the running build — exactly the same conclusion as the CLI bypass (D13): *enforce where the software runs, not where it is fetched.* A nightly build whose license does not permit nightly must refuse to run (or degrade), because nothing stopped it being installed. - The CLI has its own channel identity too — `main.channel` is baked at build time and `workroom update --channel` is user-facing — so the same gate applies there, per D13. ### Phase 3 — enforcement UX (app + CLI) - `add-project` (and whichever action the tier limits) fails with a clear, actionable message naming the limit and how to lift it. - **Over-limit is a hard block** (D16): the tool refuses the limited operations until the user is back under the limit. The copy must say what removal actually means — `delete-project` is **config-only** by default (`--from-disk` is opt-in), so unregistering a project leaves every file untouched on disk. "Remove a project from Workroom to continue. Your files stay where they are." - **Deadlock escape hatch, load-bearing.** While blocked, `delete-project`, `list` and `delete-project --from-disk` must all keep working, and the app must still launch and render the sidebar. Otherwise the only way out of the block sits behind the block. Pin this with tests on both products — it is the single most likely way a hard block ships broken. - The app surfaces the same state as UI, not a raw CLI error string. - Both read one entitlement reader, so they cannot disagree about what is allowed. ### Phase 4 — analytics **Snapshot** (D10), emitted at the end of the first *successful* `AppStore.load` (`Core/AppStore.swift:2344`), guarded by a static once-flag. The flag is load-bearing: `WorkroomApp.swift:54-59` documents that SwiftUI "mints one window — and one fresh `AppStore` — per `WindowSeed`", and ⌘N opens a new seed. A failed load emits nothing and leaves the flag unset, so a later successful reload can still emit (D9) — otherwise a broken CLI read would be recorded as a user with no projects. Set the flag **after** the consent check, not before, so enabling analytics later in the same process is not permanently suppressed. **Coarse action events** (D10) at real interaction points: inspector section opened, diff mode switched, workroom created, VCS action run, pane split. Behaviour, not settings — the snapshot alone measures configuration, which was Codex's sharpest hit. **Typed payloads, no generic value container.** Codex is right that `AnalyticsValue.string(String)` accepts any string, so a `[String: AnalyticsValue]` bag is not a compile-time guarantee. Each event case carries its own typed associated values — enums and integers only, no free `String` — with an explicit wire encoder. That is what actually makes it impossible to attach a repo path, branch, bookmark, workroom label, commit message, file name or terminal line. **Sink.** `URLSession` POST to codaset, authenticated by the license key. Constraints: - **`URLSessionConfiguration.ephemeral`, caching disabled.** A default session uses the shared URL cache, cookie storage and credential storage. - One in-memory retry after a short delay, then silent drop (D7). Launch is exactly when the network is least likely to be up (cold wake, wifi reconnecting), so a single attempt would systematically lose that whole category rather than a random sample. - **A per-emit random `event_id`** (generated in memory, never persisted) sent as an idempotency key, with a unique index server-side. Without it the retry double-counts whenever the server accepted the first POST but the response was lost. - Off the main thread. Never surfaces an error to the user. **Counts are licensing's job now.** Enforcement cannot cap what it does not count, so project and workroom counts arrive with the license check-in as exact numbers. Analytics does not carry them, and `CountBucket` is not needed (D8 superseded). ### Testability — inject the seams Compile-time build flavour, `XCTest` env detection and global statics make "every branch" untestable as drafted. `Analytics` takes injected **build identity**, **consent provider**, **sink factory** and **launch-session state**, defaulting to the real ones. Same seam `SentryConfig.defaultEnvironment(nightly:debug:)` already uses (`SentryConfig.swift:67`), and the same reason `UITestFixture` exists. ## Files **codaset** (JJ repo) — `app/models/license.rb`, `app/models/analytics_event.rb`, `app/controllers/api/licenses_controller.rb`, `app/controllers/api/analytics_controller.rb`, migrations, a retention job, deploy config, `config/routes.rb`. **workroom CLI (Go)** — new `internal/license/` (token verify, cache, grace), enforcement in `internal/workroom/` create paths and `cmd/add-project`. **macapp** — `Core/BuildIdentity.swift` (hoisted from `SentryConfig`), `Core/AnalyticsEvent.swift`, `Core/Analytics.swift`, `Core/AnalyticsHTTPSink.swift`, `Core/LicenseState.swift`; edits to `Core/DefaultsKeys.swift`, `Core/SentryConfig.swift`, `Core/AppStore.swift:2344`, `Views/SettingsView.swift:178`. New Swift files need `make app-generate`. **website** — a privacy policy page, linked from the app. ## Tests - **REGRESSION (mandatory):** hoisting `defaultEnvironment` out of `SentryConfig` modifies working behaviour. Moved tests keep asserting all three outputs, plus one pinning that nightly still tags `nightly` — that mislabelling is the documented WORKROOM-2B confusion (`SentryConfig.swift:57-63`). - **Go:** entitlement token verify (valid / tampered / expired / clock-skewed), TTL expiry, enforcement at the limit boundary (n-1, n, n+1), offline behaviour, **sticky revocation survives relaunch while offline**, **limit lowered below usage enters `over_limit`**, and — critically — **`delete-project` and `list` still work while blocked** (the deadlock escape hatch). - **Rails (minitest + `fixture_kit`):** register, re-register idempotency, check-in updates `last_seen_at`, a limit edit reaches the next token, a revoked license returns an explicit revoked response, rate limit trips, unknown event name rejected, unknown property key rejected, duplicate `event_id` rejected, cascade delete removes a license's events, retention job deletes past the window. - **Swift:** consent off ⇒ spy sink never called and no session constructed; debug and XCTest ⇒ noop; once-flag set after the consent check, not before; failed load ⇒ no emit and flag unset; every event case encodes to a stable name; `URLProtocol`-stubbed sink for 200 / non-2xx / transport error / retry-succeeds / teardown-before-retry. - **XCUITest**, scoped to the new class only (never the full suite; `make app-uitest` ignores `APP_TEST_FLAGS`, so call `xcodebuild -only-testing:/`): the Settings toggle flips and persists, matched by `accessibilityIdentifier` — XCUITest cannot match a `Form` `Toggle` by label. ## Failure modes | Path | Failure | Test | Handled | User sees | |---|---|---|---|---| | Registration | Offline on first launch | yes | grace/unregistered state | clear state, app still works | | Entitlement | Token expired, still offline | yes | grace window, then block | "reconnect to continue" | | Entitlement | Tampered token | yes | signature verify fails | treated as unlicensed | | Entitlement | Revoked, then goes offline | yes | sticky revocation flag | stays revoked | | Entitlement | Limit lowered below usage | yes | `over_limit` hard block | "remove a project to continue" | | Enforcement | Blocked with no way out | yes | delete/list stay allowed | escape hatch works | | Enforcement | CLI and app disagree | yes | one shared reader | n/a by construction | | Analytics emit | Fires twice via ⌘N | yes | once-flag | nothing (correct) | | Analytics emit | Load failed ⇒ zero counts | yes | no emit, flag unset | nothing (correct) | | Sink | Cold wake, no wifi | yes | 1 retry, drop | nothing — silent by design | | Sink | Response lost after accept | yes | `event_id` idempotency | nothing | | Ingest | Flooded by a script | yes | per-key rate limit | nothing | ## NOT in scope - **CLI analytics** — the CLI enforces licensing but emits no behaviour events. Explicit non-goal. - **Anonymous analytics** — D14 chose identified. The anonymity posture from D3/D4 is superseded. - **Gating `SentryConfig.start()` behind a user toggle** — crash reporting stays unconditional with no user control. Raised in review and **explicitly declined**, not deferred. If it is ever revisited: the gate must wrap the `start()` call itself, never filter events, because the crash handler installs before anything can crash (`SentryConfig.swift:16-20`). - **Pricing and tier design** — this plan assumes limits exist; it does not choose them. - **A licensing design review** — this was an analytics review that discovered licensing. Phases 0-3 deserve their own review before implementation. ## What already exists (reused, not rebuilt) | Need | Existing code | Reused? | |---|---|---| | Build identity | `SentryConfig.swift:67`, `:76` | Yes — hoisted to `BuildIdentity` | | Privacy-gate pattern (off ⇒ no request) | `loadRemoteAvatars`, `DefaultsKeys.swift:101` | Yes | | Nightly identity | `ReleaseChannel.isNightlyBuild`, `ReleaseChannel.swift:67` | Yes | | VCS kind per project | `Project.vcs`, `Models.swift:53` | Yes | | Test-only seam | `XCTestConfigurationFilePath`, `WorkroomApp.swift:42` | Yes | | Settings `Form` pane | `GeneralSettingsPane`, `SettingsView.swift:178` | Yes — no new pane | | Log subsystem | `"com.developwithstyle.workroom"` (literal, `LibGit2.swift:28`) | Yes | | App↔CLI transport | the `--json` envelope (`cmd/json.go`) | Yes — entitlement rides it | | Rate limiting | Rails 8 built-in `rate_limit` | Yes — no gem | | Generic CRUD | `ControllerConcerns::Crud` (codaset) | No — API ingest is not CRUD | ## Parallelization | Lane | Steps | Modules | Depends on | |---|---|---|---| | — | Phase 0 deploy codaset | codaset deploy config | — | | A | Phase 1 licensing server | codaset `app/`, `config/` | Phase 0 | | B | `BuildIdentity` hoist + analytics schema | `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/` | — | | C | Phase 2 entitlement reader | `internal/license/` (Go) | Phase 1 (token format) | | D | Phase 3 enforcement + Phase 4 sink | `cmd/`, `internal/workroom/`, `macapp/` | B, C | **Launch B in parallel with Phase 0 + A** — it touches only `macapp/Core/` and needs no server. C waits on A for the token format. D waits on both. Lanes B and D both touch `macapp/` — sequential within that directory, so do not run them concurrently in separate worktrees. ## Verification 1. `make cli-build && make cli-test && make cli-lint` (Go). 2. `make app-build && make app-format && make app-lint`, then `make app-test` — read pass/fail from the `.xcresult` via `xcresulttool`, the summary is hidden under Xcode 26. 3. codaset: `bin/ci` (setup + rubocop + audits + tests + seed replant). 4. XCUITest scoped to the new class only. 5. End to end against a staging codaset: fresh install registers, entitlement caches, `add-project` blocks at the limit **from the terminal as well as the app**, behaviour events arrive with the right license, a duplicate `event_id` is rejected, and the retention job deletes past the window. 6. Manual privacy audit: `log stream --predicate 'subsystem == "com.developwithstyle.workroom"'` (a hardcoded literal, NOT the bundle id — Debug and Release share it). Every property must be an enum, integer or version string. If anything in that log looks like it came off your disk, the schema is wrong. A `nettop shows zero connections` acceptance test would be **void** — Sentry and the licensing check-in both make network calls, so absence cannot be attributed to analytics. Verify at the request level or against an isolated endpoint instead. ## Implementation Tasks - [ ] **T0 (P1)** — codaset — deploy it. Verify: `/up` returns 200 over HTTPS on a real domain - [ ] **T1 (P1)** — macapp — hoist build identity out of `SentryConfig` into `Core/BuildIdentity.swift` - [ ] **T2 (P1)** — codaset — `License`, register + check endpoints, signed token - [ ] **T3 (P1)** — CLI — shared entitlement reader, 7-day TTL, sticky revocation - [ ] **T4 (P1)** — macapp + CLI — hard-block enforcement UX + deadlock escape hatch - [ ] **T5 (P2)** — macapp — typed event schema, no generic value container - [ ] **T6 (P2)** — macapp — `Analytics` façade with injected seams - [ ] **T7 (P2)** — macapp — emit at first *successful* load, flag set after consent - [ ] **T8 (P2)** — macapp — ephemeral-session sink, one retry, `event_id` - [ ] **T9 (P2)** — codaset — `analytics_events`, cascade delete, retention job - [ ] **T10 (P2)** — website + app — privacy policy, honest toggle copy ## Review status Eng review: **ISSUES_OPEN** — 18 issues, 0 critical gaps, 1 unresolved decision. Outside voice (Codex): 12 findings, 11 folded, 1 rejected on evidence. **Unresolved:** grace-window semantics beyond the 7-day token TTL are undefined — whether `grace` is a distinct state after `expired` or the TTL *is* the grace, how long it lasts, and what remains usable inside it. Phase 2 is not buildable until this is answered, and it cannot be tested until it is specified.

Posted: https://github.com/joelmoss/workroom/issues/92#issuecomment-5214474180

Short summary up top with the three findings worth reading, full plan in a collapsed `<details>` block so the issue stays scannable.

The issue's own wording added something the review had missed — **available release channels** as a second restriction dimension. I worked it into the plan before posting, because it lands the same way the CLI-bypass finding did:

- Nightly isn't a picker option, it's a **separate product** with its own bundle id and DMG. There's no picker to restrict.
- GitHub Releases are public, so the **download can't be gated** — anyone can pull any DMG with Sparkle uninvolved.
- So a channel restriction is only enforceable **at run time**, by the entitlement check inside the running build. Same rule as the CLI: enforce where the software runs, not where it's fetched.

The plan file at `~/.claude/plans/what-are-the-options-wise-dragonfly.md` has the same content plus the review report, if you want it locally.
